The two countries have ramped up long-range attacks in recent months, driving up the civilian death toll on both sides in the four-and-a-half-year war. The massive missile attack on Kyiv struck residential areas and warehouses, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko wrote on Telegram. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A medical facility and an educational institution were also damaged, according to the city's military administration. Klitschko later said the death toll in the capital had risen to 12, with 33 people wounded. An attack in the Brovary district of the broader Kyiv region also killed one man and wounded another, Kyiv regional governor Tymur Tkachenko said. It was unclear whether that death was included in Klitschko's tally. "One industrial facility has been damaged. All relevant services are on site, working to extinguish the fire," Tkachenko added. Ukraine's air force had warned of Russian "Kalibr" missiles in the vicinity of the village of Kagarlyk within the Kyiv region, heading towards the capital. Advertisement Advertisement The attacks also prompted security responses in neighbouring NATO member states. Poland's military command said it had mobilised aircraft and activated air defences aimed at protecting its airspace, particularly in areas bordering Ukraine. Romania's defence ministry said radar systems detected aerial targets near the Ukrainian border overnight, prompting the scrambling of two Spanish fighter jets deployed on NATO missions and a Romanian air force helicopter. The ministry said a drone entered Romanian airspace near Galati before crashing in an unpopulated area in the country of Tulcea. Russia also reported a large Ukrainian drone attack. Advertisement Advertisement Moscow's Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 250 drones had flown toward the Moscow region between Wednesday night and Thursday morning, with most destroyed at a significant distance from the capital itself. "Twenty-eight drones were destroyed in the Moscow region," Sobyanin said. A Telekom ezzel reagált arra, hogy a fradi szurkolóinak egy csoportja olyan molinókat feszített ki a meccsen, mint hogy „ha bántod a Fradit, halott leszel” . „Számunkra a Fradi szenvedély és siker. Kitartás és erő. Múlt és jövő. Csillogó arcok, pacsik, összekacsintások és barátságok. Közösségek, melyek összetartanak, segítenek, támogatnak és felemelnek. Közös élmények. A Fradi nem fenyegetés, agresszió, vagy félelemkeltés, és semmi esetre sem tiszteletlenség vagy kirekesztés.” „Éppen ezért, a Magyar Telekom, mint a Ferencvárosi Torna Club fő támogatója elhatárolódik minden, a szurkolók egyes csoportjai által, a Ferencváros – Újpest hétvégi magyar bajnoki labdarúgó mérkőzésen, a Groupama Arénában használt transzparenstől és megnyilvánulástól.” „Ezek éles ellentétben állnak azokkal az értékekkel, melyeket a Magyar Telekom márka magáénak vall és hisz, és a többi szurkoló számára sem támogatja a családbarát, biztonságos és sportszerű környezet megteremtését a lelátókon.” – írta a Telekom. A fradisták molinója. Forrás: Magyar Hang A vállalat azt is írta, hogy hétfőn hivatalos állásfoglalást kért a Ferencvárosi Torna Clubtól és a Groupama Arénát üzemeltető Sportfive Hungary Kft.-től arról, milyen intézkedéseket és megelőző lépéseket terveznek annak érdekében, hogy az „agresszív megnyilvánulásokat” távol tartsák a lelátóktól. „Szponzorációnkkal továbbra is a hazai viszonylatban kiemelkedő népszerűségű és nagy múltra visszatekintő klubot támogatjuk – annak sportolóival, utánpótlás játékosaival, edzőivel, egyéb munkatársaival és azon szurkolóival – akik számára az alapvető emberi értékek ugyanolyan fontosak, mint nekünk” – zárja a bejegyzést a cég, arra utalva, hogy továbbra is szponzorálni fogja a csapatot. https://www.politico.eu/article/russian-.text: KYIV — The local governor of Russia’s Samara region blamed Ukraine for an early morning drone attack that struck an oil refinery in Novokuibyshevsk city. “In the course of terrorist attacks on the civil infrastructure of our region and country, the vile enemy from Kyiv launched a record number of drones. There were no casualties, which is the most important thing,” Samara Governor Viacheslav Fedorischev said in a statement on Russian state messaging app Max. Russian air defense forces shot down 1,043 Ukrainian drones over Samara, and 18 other Russian regions overnight, Moscow’s Ministry of Defense reported Friday. Advertisement Advertisement Fedorischev asked locals not to reveal what was struck, but independent Russian media channel Astra reported a fire at the local oil refinery, which produces jet fuel for the Russian army. Novokuibyshevsk oil refinery can produce about 8.8 million metric tons of oil per year, according to Russian oil company Rosneft . The Wall Street Journal reported Thursday that Kyiv had agreed to pause strikes on Russian oil refineries under pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump. The unofficial halt is expected, according to the report, to last until after the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3. Ukraine had paused drone strikes on Russian oil refineries for 72 hours when Trump announced an energy ceasefire earlier this month. But the Kremlin kept bombarding Ukrainian energy infrastructure. “That didn’t help. There was all kinds of rhetoric, and no one thanked us for those three days,” Zelenskyy told reporters in Kyiv earlier this week. As of Friday morning, Ukraine has not taken responsibility for the latest strike — though there was some trolling from the Ukrainian military-industrial complex. “Little drone, how did you end up there? The Novokuibyshevsk oil refinery welcomes guests from Ukraine,” Ukrainian defense company Fire Point — which produces long-range drones used by Kyiv to bomb targets in Russia — said in a morning Telegram post. Russia also attacked Ukraine with ballistic missiles and more than 100 drones overnight, killing one person in Kyiv and leaving 350,000 people without electricity in Dnipro. https://www.azernews.az/nation/266880.ht.text: Azerbaijan, Estonia explore new opportunities for cooperation in ICT sector 5 November 2026 17:40 (UTC+04:00) Ulviyya Poladova Read more Azerbaijan and Estonia discussed opportunities to expand cooperation in information and communication technologies (ICT). Azerbaijan’s Minister of Digital Development and Transport, Rashad Nabiyev, shared the details in a post on social media X. "We held a roundtable meeting with a delegation of IT companies organised by the Estonian Association of Information Technology and Telecommunications (ITL). During the meeting, we briefed Estonian companies on the latest developments in Azerbaijan’s digitalisation efforts, the newly adopted legislative package and the opportunities available in the technology sector. We also discussed ways to expand cooperation in ICT, opportunities for Estonian companies to enter the Azerbaijani market and prospects for implementing joint projects," Nabiyev wrote. It should be noted that Nabiyev also took part in the fourth meeting of the Azerbaijan-Estonia Intergovernmental Commission held the previous day. The meeting was attended by Estonia’s Minister of Justice and Digital Affairs Liisa-Ly Pakosta and Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna. The sides discussed ways to strengthen cooperation in transport, logistics, trade, digital development and innovation. Article content A British national was among the killed, according to Polish police chief, Marek Boron, and five foreigners were among the wounded in hospital, the authorities said. “Two people who have not yet been identified,” Boron said referring to the victims killed. Britain’s Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was “shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting.” “My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence,” he wrote on X . The suspect – a Polish citizen born in 2002 – drove a car onto Krakow’s Main Market Square and began shooting at random people, said police. Two officers were wounded as they tried to stop the man, the police said, before shooting the suspect who was later detained and taken to a hospital. Article content An AFP reporter at the scene saw ambulances and multiple police cars as police cordoned off the area – one of Poland’s landmark tourist hotspots popular with locals and foreign visitors. “Everything suggests that the perpetrator held very, very radical views. A number of weapons were found in the car he was driving,” Kierwinski said. “Everything suggests that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies” and held “ultra-nationalist views,” he added. The man was wearing military-style clothing at the time of the attack, said Kierwinski. Tusk praises ‘heroic’ police Andrzej Fijolek, spokesman for the chief of police, said the attacker had used a semi-automatic rifle similar to the American AR-15. The authorities have not yet disclosed the nationalities of all the victims of the attack, Poland’s deadliest shooting since the fall of communism in 1989. “Our highest praise goes to the heroic police officers who risked their lives in the line of duty,” Tusk said . Article content On Saturday evening, AFP reporters saw the usually bustling Main Market Square sealed off, with heavily armed police and forensic investigators inspecting the site of the attack. Witnesses told AFP they saw people take refuge in shops and restaurants in the streets around the Main Market Square. “I saw a man shooting at people and walking around the square,” Annette, a woman in her sixties, told AFP. “It’s a tragedy for Krakow, we’ve never seen anything like this before,” she added. “We were at Auschwitz today. And it was only when we got here that we realised what had happened,” Stella, a 22-year-old tourist from Rennes, northwest France, told AFP, referring to the Nazi German Auschwitz-Birkenau concentration camp near Krakow. “It’s very frightening to think that there are still risks in Europe – risks of a terrorist nature,” she told AFP. ‘Dramatic events’ Deadly shootings are extremely rare in Poland, a European Union and NATO member of 38 million people. Article content But the country has been on high alert following a series of stabbings in October, which Tusk denounced as a “cult of violence.” Warsaw, a staunch ally of Ukraine since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, has repeatedly warned of Russian sabotage and hybrid warfare on Polish soil, accusations rejected by Moscow. Poland is also seeing a sharp rise in the number of firearms licences. In 2025, more than 50,000 new licences were issued, bringing the total to 411,000, according to police figures. The historic city of Krakow in southern Poland was once the country’s capital and attracts millions of tourists every year. In 2025, it was visited by 16.2 million people, the city said. Poland’s conservative-nationalist president Karol Nawrocki said on X he was awaiting “a full explanation of the circumstances surrounding these dramatic events.” “The safety of Poles is an absolute priority,” he added. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky offered his condolences , saying that “Ukraine stands in solidarity with Poland and the Polish people. People have the right to safety.” German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on X that “Germany stands shoulder to shoulder with Poland as a friend and partner during these difficult times.” The EU’s top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, described the shooting as “a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland”, adding: “My thoughts are with the victims and their families and the first responders.” U.S. Ambassador to Poland Tom Rose, posting on X , said: “America stands with Poland at this dark hour as Poland stands with her beloved citizens of Krakow.” Article content Share this article in your social network Share this Story : Toronto Sun Copy Link Email X Reddit Pinterest LinkedIn Tumblr Comments You must be logged in to join the discussion or read more comments.
